findings.claim: hub_get catches only URLError, OSError and ValueError. http.client.HTTPException subclasses raised by getresponse() or response.read() (IncompleteRead, BadStatusLine) are not HubError or GhError. main() catches only (GhError, KeyError, ValueError) and writes files after the loop, so one truncated Hub response aborts the whole run with a traceback and writes no reviews, including the GitHub ones. The docstring promises the repository is 'reported and skipped'.
findings.disposition: repaired in 41f53cb1: hub_get also catches http.client.HTTPException

findings.claim: The allowlist is rule-, path- and line-scoped, but it ignores the value. A pin line holding any bare 40-hex value is exempt: uppercase (not a git commit id), or free text such as 'sourcegraph legacy access token <hex>'. That is exactly the sourcegraph-access-token rule's bare [a-fA-F0-9]{40} alternative, the legacy token shape. Only underscore forms (sgp_...) stay caught. The 2026-09-23 entry required one lowercase 40-hex id, and the ai-memory entry pins values. This one could require \b[0-9a-f]{40}\b or pin the 60 reviewed ids.
findings.disposition: repaired in 9522b5cf: the allowlist pins the 39 reviewed commit ids by value (secret target) instead of a pin-line shape, so any other 40-hex value, an uppercase variant or an sgp_ token stays detected (test_d3/test_d4)

findings.claim: by_repo is keyed by slug(), which for a Hugging Face URL returns the whole lowercased URL. HUB_MODEL accepts both https://huggingface.co/Org/M and .../Org/M/. If two layers keep the same model with and without the trailing slash, the tool writes two hash-suffixed reviews and exits 0, instead of one review whose layers names both. GitHub URLs are normalized by slug().
findings.disposition: repaired in 41f53cb1: survivors are grouped by repository_key (hf:<namespace>/<name>), and make_result.py matches reviews without trailing slashes

findings.claim: The YAML front-matter strip requires the card to start with '---'. Upstream huggingface_hub repocard.REGEX_YAML_BLOCK allows leading whitespace (^\s*---) and requires the closing '---' to end its line. A card with a leading newline keeps its metadata block, which is then excerpted, contrary to the docstring.
findings.disposition: repaired in 41f53cb1: the card metadata block is stripped with huggingface_hub's repocard.REGEX_YAML_BLOCK

The limit-3 times '04:15Z' (re-sign-in), '04:17Z to 05:35Z' (fit queue) and 'about 03:57Z' (runner change) appear only in the limit text copied into lanes.json and the manifest. The 8 never-started fit jobs have no started or finished times in returns.json. Only the 03:47-03:55Z interval is backed by job timestamps.

findings.claim: Limit 4 says that of '46 seeds that name a repository' no worker proposed 11, but the count is GitHub-only without saying so. The agents-models-workers seed names Hugging Face model repositories. One of them, Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, was proposed by no worker, including the capped 'dropped' lists, yet it is not among the 11. findings.claim: The session's WebSearch budget (200 calls) ran out at 04:10:13Z and nothing in the record said so: 154 calls returned results and 46 were capped, in 30 workers, so the refutation phase, the critic and the follow-up round ran without WebSearch. votes/identity-provenance/3/facts refuted databento/databento-python for want of a search. refute-fit:agent-sdks was capped, yet agent-sdks counted as clean. The lane's budgets exceed the cap, and convert.py did not flag capped calls.
findings.verification: Reproduced from the transcripts by pairing every WebSearch tool_use with its tool_result: 200 calls, 154 with results, 46 capped (200 of 200), first 04:10:13.805Z, last 11:55:57.115Z. The cap and its env variable are documented (tools-reference, 'Session search limit'; env-vars), and the 2.1.283 client sets the default to 200.
findings.disposition: repaired in 1bd2416b and this record: child-usage.mjs counts capped calls; convert.py makes each capped worker a web_search_capped retained failure (the critic's for every layer), so every layer is reopened; make_result.py refuses uncovered capped workers; lane limit 10, the README section 'WebSearch session cap', a ledger note, and the harness README and recipe on raising the cap

findings.claim: The ledger note said the nine layers' proposals are recorded as refuted by the missing vote, against the incident log's 'never as refuted-by-absence'. 27 proposals that passed facts and the Claude fit refuter sit under refuted, and build_inputs.py (previous_sweep.refuted) and saturation_ledger.py (adjudicated_repos) treat them as adjudicated.
findings.verification: Reproduced: 27 refuted entries in 9 layers whose only refuting vote is a missing GPT-6 member.
findings.disposition: repaired in 1bd2416b and this record: refutes_on_merit and refuted_by_absence read the missing marker, adjudicated_repos leaves such entries out, build_inputs.py lists them as not_adjudicated, convert.py names them in each layer's votes_note, and the ledger note says so. The offered alternative, collecting the nine GPT-6 fit votes before appending, was not taken: those would be votes of a new model run, not of this run; the verdict wave takes the 27 as its first candidates for a second-family fit vote.
